proc_direct.title: Large award without competition
proc_direct.text: A contract was awarded by direct award, single tender action or waiver rather than competition. These are lawful in defined circumstances but deserve a reason.

proc_late.title: Published long after the award
proc_late.text: The award notice appeared months after the award date, so the public could not see it in good time.

proc_estimate.title: Award far from the advertised value
proc_estimate.text: The awarded value is much higher (or lower) than the estimate the buyer first published.

proc_long.title: Very long contract
proc_long.text: A contract running for more than ten years.

proc_split.title: Repeat awards to one supplier in a short window
proc_split.text: The same buyer made several separate awards to the same supplier within a few months, which can be legitimate or can be a contract split to stay below a limit.

proc_conc.title: One supplier dominates a buyer's spend
proc_conc.text: A single supplier received a large share of a buyer's awarded value.

proc_implausible.title: Value looks like a data-entry error
proc_implausible.text: A single award of £10bn or more is far larger than almost any real contract on Contracts Finder (often an extra zero, or a framework's lifetime ceiling typed as a contract value). It is left out of every total and chart on this page so one entry cannot distort them.
